prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms that made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration unchanged: a single prize part on B036 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed no disagreement on the ballot, so the case has to rest on content, not on the count of first places. The chain from proglucagon processing and the identification of the active GLP-1 peptides, through human incretin physiology and glucose-dependent insulin secretion, to central satiety and gastric effects, and on to therapies with independent randomized outcome benefit in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease, is complete and stable. Nobody has questioned maturity. On the chair's central question, the citation should reward the discovery of what the hormone is and does, including its active forms. The drug engineering is a decisive consequence, and the citation wording acknowledges it. A single part is sufficient. I see no second achievement on the shortlist whose allocation is clean enough to add, and a second part would only be justified by a candidate that stands on its own merits, not by a wish to include more work.
statement.case_against: The allocation is imperfect and I do not think it can be made otherwise. Knudsen's engineering of long-acting analogues is what made the therapy practical, Habener sits outside the credited names although he has a real claim to the early peptide work, and Mojsov's priority on the active peptide is contested and not verified in the supplied evidence. My recollection of the chronology is from memory only. If the committee decides that the prize should mark the transformation of care and not the discovery, my configuration is the weaker one and the Drucker, Holst and Knudsen version becomes the better choice. I have not seen an argument for that framing that persuades me, but I cannot rule it out. The citation will inevitably leave out a defensible contributor, and the record should say so.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, but says the opening configuration would be better if the Committee values the transformation of care as much as the discovery, and suggests the unfolded protein response as a cleaner option if GLP-1 allocation stalls.
responses.response: I share your move and your stated condition, so I will answer the condition directly. I do not think the allocation has stalled, because the difficulty is the choice of third name and not whether a defensible configuration exists. The physiology framing is the better one for this prize. The identification of the active peptide and the human physiology define the target that Knudsen's analogues were designed around, and the citation can name the therapeutic consequence without crediting the engineering. I would not use B006 as a replacement for B036. Its two-name allocation is clean, but its clinical impact is still indirect, and exchanging a complete discovery-to-therapy arc for a cleaner allocation would be trading scientific strength for convenience.

responses.point: Sandberg moved to the Mojsov trio, framing the prize as a discovery of physiology and the active peptide, and notes that the unanimity on B036 says nothing about the ordering of the remaining candidates or whether a second part is wanted.
responses.response: I agree that unanimity on the first place tells us nothing about the rest, and that is why I do not want to add a second part for its own sake. Of the candidates that would pair with B036, B042 has the strongest influence on circuit neuroscience, and I should repeat that this field is close to mine. As you note, it would need a decision to credit a tool and then to reduce six names to three, and I still cannot see that reduction made on discovery grounds. If the committee wants a second part, I would sooner see that argument made openly for B006 than accept an unresolved allocation for B042. I do not think we need to settle it to proceed, because B036 stands alone.

responses.point: Perlmann shares the trio, asks that Habener's absence be recorded openly, and regards the unfolded protein response as unable to combine with GLP-1 within the three-person limit.
responses.response: I agree that Habener's absence should be recorded in the deliberation, not hidden in the citation, and I would put it in the record together with the contested status of Mojsov's priority. Your point on the three-person limit also matters for the second-part question: Mori and Walter cannot be added to the trio without exceeding three unique people, so B006 can enter only as a replacement. That is a stronger test than a pairing. I do not think B006 passes it against B036 on present evidence. On your earlier comment on my ranking of cGAS-STING and TOR, I accept your reading that the therapeutic validation and the competing claims make both premature, and that does not change my configuration.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, keeps the physiology trio but accepts that a physiology-centred trio may be read as under-crediting industrial drug development that reached patients, and asks whether a two-part prize would be better.
responses.response: I take the risk of being read as under-crediting development seriously, and I do not wish to dismiss it from the chair's side of the table. My answer is that a prize for physiology is not a prize for the drugs, and the citation text can state that incretin-based therapy followed from these discoveries. I would apply the same principle to other candidates, which is the point of my round-1 comment on B026: where credited names cover development and earlier discoveries lie outside them, I am reluctant, and I should be equally reluctant here if the trio covered only the product. Because it covers the peptide, its physiology and its actions, I think the principle is applied consistently. I would not use a two-part prize to mend the Knudsen question, because B036 cannot hold four names and a second part would add three more, which exceeds the limit.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius places B031 (TNF blockade) and B047 (CAR-T) among her alternatives and asks whether the gaps in B026 and B047 credit would disqualify them, and whether TNF blockade is late recognition or fully mature.
responses.response: On the consistency question you raise, I think a credit gap outside the named people does weaken a candidacy when the missing work is the discovery and the named work is the development, which is why I hesitate over B026 and B031 as the supplied names stand. B047 has the same concern because Eshhar is missing, and unresolved solid-tumour and long-term toxicity questions also bear on its maturity. On B031, I regard it as clinically mature but not yet allocated cleanly, and I cannot say whether it is late recognition because I have only the credited pair and not the cytokine work. I do not see any of these three overtaking B042 or B006 as my alternatives today, and none of them is a reason to alter the B036 configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the third laureate should be Mojsov or Knudsen, which depends on whether the Committee treats the prize as marking physiology or the transformation of care. I have not verified the priority claims.
Habener's claim to the early peptide work sits outside the credited names, so any trio represents the discovery incompletely. I would record this in the deliberation.

If B036 stalls, whether B006 (clean allocation, indirect clinical effect) or B042 (broad influence, six names, a tool) is the better substitute. I am not confident on this and I have not changed my alternatives.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. My documented connections (the 2019 synthesis with Grillner, work with Ernfors, and a 2009 paper with Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons) do not concern any credited person. My motor-circuit field is close to B042, which I list only as an alternative; this is topical proximity and not a documented tie, and I would flag it again if B042 became a serious option. Shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation with other members and with candidates is not treated as a conflict. Unchanged from round 1.
